name: sdsaati/tools
summary: A personal dotfiles and day-to-day tooling repository -- alacritty, tmux, zsh and xorg configuration committed alongside a whole Codon installation under a .codon directory, which is where the installer puts it in a home folder. Seventy-one stdlib files are present and no Codon source of the owner's own. The repo shows Codon installed, not Codon used.
why_codon: No claim; the README covers terminal tooling. Inferred from a committed home-directory .codon install with no own source that the owner installed Codon and the dotfiles repo captured it.
note: An accidental entry in the strict sense -- the install was swept into a dotfiles repo. Kept under ruling 3, which admits vendored installs, and scored at its true own-source size of zero.

name: mect_1ano
summary: A university coursework archive covering a first year of study, one directory per subject. The Codon installation sits inside the AAD directory's first practical, seventy-two stdlib files deep, with none of the student's own Codon source committed beside it.
why_codon: No claim. Inferred from the install sitting under an algorithms-and-data-structures practical that Codon was introduced in that course exercise.
note: Second course found using Codon, distinct from UVic CSC427 and taught in Portuguese.

name: mpearrow/codon-site
summary: A copy of Codon's documentation site, carrying the install, FAQ, changelog, roadmap, NumPy and Python-interop pages as they stood when taken.
why_codon: A documentation copy; no claim of its own.

name: mpearrow/codon-docs
summary: A second copy of Codon's documentation by the same owner, built as a Hugo site with rendered HTML output committed alongside the markdown.
why_codon: A documentation copy; no claim of its own.

name: mpearrow/codon-md
summary: A third copy of Codon's documentation by the same owner, this one built as an mdBook with the rendered book committed. Three formats of the same source, which is a single person's format experiment rather than three independent mirrors.
why_codon: A documentation copy; no claim of its own.
note: The three mpearrow repos are one effort in three output formats. Counting them as three mirrors overstates independent interest.

name: exaloop.io
summary: Exaloop's own marketing site. First-party rather than a mirror, and the place where the project's public framing of Codon is written.
note: First-party, not a third-party mirror. Should probably sit with the anchors rather than in the mirror class.

name: awesome-architecture-mds
summary: A collection of machine-generated architecture write-ups for open-source projects. Codon has two, an onboarding overview and a JIT-compiler walkthrough, produced by a documentation tool rather than by the project.
why_codon: Carries generated architecture documentation for Codon among many projects.
note: Machine-authored documentation about Codon, flagged under ruling 6. Second machine-authored entry after PL-ultimate-llm, and the second channel by which Codon reaches model-generated material, alongside llmref.
